entries.test: Production records, raw footage, and testimony would establish whether Tesla's 2016 demo was staged rather than one unedited autonomous run.
entries.note: The hedge concerns the evidence for a concrete historical event.

entries.test: Documented autonomous journeys through January 18, 2023 would establish whether any car completed an LA-to-NYC drive without human assistance or intervention.
entries.note: The claim is bounded by the publication date.

entries.test: Contemporaneous autonomous-driving performance evidence and public statements would establish the relative difficulty of highway driving and whether anyone claimed to be close to an intervention-free LA-to-NYC trip off the Interstate.
entries.note: “Doing that” refers to the LA-to-NYC journey; the proposition broadens it to off-Interstate driving generally.

entries.test: Court transcripts, employee roles, and human-factors safety research would establish the reported unfamiliarity and the necessity of human-factors engineering for systems requiring human participation.
entries.note: The claimed unfamiliarity is grounded in public testimony, rather than an inaccessible private belief.

entries.test: Reporting, contracts, pay records, and worker testimony would establish OpenAI's use of outsourced labor under the low-pay and harmful working conditions described.
entries.note: The surrounding account gives “sweatshops” a concrete factual basis that can be examined.

entries.test: Published development methods and labor records would establish the scale of human work used to train ChatGPT's filtering of harmful content.
entries.note: The context concerns human labor supporting development and filtering, without asserting live human review of every response.

entries.test: Contractor records, compensation records, and worker accounts would establish the amount of Kenyan annotation work, its graphic content, and whether workers earned less than $2 per hour.
entries.note: “A bunch” describes an amount; “much of” implies a substantial share of all filtering work that the source does not establish.

entries.test: Goodside's published Claude conversations and independent verification of their factual assertions would establish whether Claude readily generated hallucinations.
entries.note: The comparison identifies the same failure mode, not an equal measured hallucination rate.
The errors are checkable separately, but “first casualty” supplies no shared criterion for qualifying harm or the relevant comparison group.
“Real AI” has no agreed operational meaning here, so readers could select different systems to test.
Neither “real AI” nor its required learning capability is specified sufficiently to identify a shared test.
The contrast between “shallow data” and “deep understanding” does not identify an agreed causal variable or comparison.

entries.test: Public studies and documented deployments would establish whether choices among AI designs cause social effects such as changes in labor demand, working conditions, or safety.
entries.note: This is broad but has a plain empirical reading: AI design decisions produce social consequences.
The proposition adds an explicit human-cost condition to a general judgment that a slower approach can be better.
